title: Phygmalion
summary: King of Tyre in Menander, in whose seventh year his sister fled and founded Carthage (Cory 1876).
description: Added from the Cory import. Display only. Cory gives reign lengths and synchronisms, not a BC year this record can sort on, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year (Cory is display-only and gives none).

reign.note: pending CFAH reference (no CFAH anchor point or Table 1 entry found for this)

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 30; Menander of Ephesus, ap. Josephus
reign.note: The edition spells the name Phygmalion.

reign.date: “In the seventh year of his reign, his sister (Dido), fled from him, and founded the city of Carthage in Libya (b.c. 878)”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 30; Menander of Ephesus, ap. Josephus
reign.note: The parenthesis "(b.c. 878)" is printed in the sentence, immediately before the Josephus citation. It is not stored as year_bc_ad. Whether it is Menander's figure or the editor's gloss is open (H2). Generations, on founding-of-carthage, prints "Sometime between 800 and 900 BC" (provisional). 878, if it is a year, falls inside that range. It does not set the sort.
